name: Perplexity.ai
tagline: A conversational AI search engine
description: Perplexity combines publicly available web data with large language models (LLMs) to generate concise, sourced answers to user queries. It retrieves and summarizes current web content, displaying inline citations that link to original sources. The tool emphasizes transparency by showing references, but users should verify results for accuracy, completeness, and bias.

name: Semantic Scholar
tagline: Free, nonprofit AI search engine for scholarly literature
description: Developed by the Allen Institute for AI, Semantic Scholar uses artificial intelligence to surface relevant, high-quality research. It includes features such as topic summaries, citation highlights, and author influence metrics. As an open, academically focused alternative to commercial AI search tools, it offers students and faculty an ethical and accessible option for exploring scholarly work.

name: OpenAlex
tagline: Open database of scholarly metadata powering AI research tools such as Litmaps and Research Rabbit
description: OpenAlex provides open data on scholarly works, authors, and institutions that power many AI-driven discovery systems, including Litmaps and Research Rabbit. Launched in 2022, it represents a major advancement in open infrastructure for academic research. It also provides a free API for use in web and AI apps.

name: Research Rabbit
tagline: Citation mapping and literature discovery tool
description: Research Rabbit helps researchers visualize connections between papers, authors, and research topics. It uses machine learning to identify similar works and recommend related studies, supporting literature review development and exploration of scholarly networks.
notes: Has not disclosed information about its underlying models or bias mitigation practices.

name: Litmaps
tagline: Citation-mapping and trend-visualization platform
description: Litmaps uses citation data and machine learning to visualize how ideas and research topics evolve over time. It helps researchers identify influential papers, emerging themes, and gaps within the scholarly conversation. Complementing tools like Research Rabbit, it emphasizes chronological connections and thematic development.
notes: Increasingly added to university library guides in 2024-2025.

name: Statista (Research AI)
tagline: Data-driven question and visualization tool
description: This feature enables users to ask data-focused questions in natural language and receive concise summaries and visualizations based on Statista's verified reports and statistics. It uses large language models (LLMs) to interpret queries and produce responses drawn solely from Statista's internal database, not external sources.
notes: Available through the SJSU Library. Transparency or bias documentation has not been provided.

name: Taylor and Francis (Journal Suggester)
tagline: AI-assisted journal recommendation tool
description: This tool helps authors identify suitable Taylor & Francis journals for their manuscripts. It uses natural language processing (NLP) to analyze a paper's title and abstract, comparing the content to published articles across Taylor & Francis journals to generate recommendations.
notes: Available through the SJSU Library. Details about training data or bias mitigation methods have not been made public.

name: Oxford English Dictionary
tagline: Natural language search enhancement (Pilot)
description: This pilot tool allows users to pose questions in natural language, which it translates into advanced dictionary queries to retrieve relevant OED entries. The AI Search Assistant does not generate new definitions but reformulates user input to improve search precision.
notes: Available through the SJSU Library. Oxford University Press has not disclosed details about the model or training data used in this pilot.

name: Elicit
tagline: AI-assisted literature-review and evidence synthesis tool
description: Elicit helps users locate and summarize scholarly papers in response to research questions. Rather than generating new text, it extracts key details such as study aims and methods, making it a reliable entry point for evidence-based exploration. Increasingly adopted in higher education since 2023, it is useful for faculty and graduate students conducting systematic or scoping reviews.

name: LumaLabs (Luma AI)
tagline: 3D capture and cinematic video generation tool
description: LumaLabs lets you turn short text prompts, images, or even 3D captures into cinematic video clips. Using neural rendering and machine learning, it generates realistic movement, depth, and lighting for professional-looking results.
notes: Free plan offers limited monthly credits; paid plans provide higher-quality output and more render time. Luma has not shared details about its training data or how it addresses bias in its models.

name: Runway (Gen-3 Alpha)
tagline: AI-powered video generation and editing platform
description: Runway's Gen-3 Alpha model can transform text, images, or audio into fast, high-quality videos with a professional finish. It supports real-time editing and motion generation, and users can experiment with both free and paid tiers.
notes: Runway reports that its models are trained on licensed and public data, though it has not disclosed specific datasets or transparency documentation. Includes a 1-minute demo video link.

name: Descript
tagline: AI-assisted video and podcast editing platform
description: Descript allows users to edit video and audio by editing text. It automatically transcribes uploaded recordings and lets users cut, move, and refine content directly in the transcript, making it ideal for creating instructional videos, lectures, or tutorials. It also supports screen recording, automatic captioning, and overdub voice correction.
notes: Offers both free and paid tiers; widely used in educational contexts, but the company has released limited details about its training data or transparency practices.

name: ElevenLabs (Voice Generator)
tagline: AI text-to-speech and voice narration tool
description: ElevenLabs is a popular tool for adding voice narration to videos and presentations without recording your own voice. It converts written text into natural-sounding speech across a range of tones and languages.
notes: Limited free plan available, with subscription options for larger projects. The company has not released information about its voice training data or safeguards against misuse.

name: Adobe Firefly (Image Generator)
tagline: AI-powered image generation using licensed and public-domain content
description: Firefly 3 generates images from text prompts using artwork contributed by consenting creators, making it more suitable for academic and professional use. The model is trained on licensed content from Adobe Stock and public-domain material.
notes: Available via SJSU Creative Cloud Campus Access. Sign in with SJSU email through the Adobe Firefly website or Adobe Creative Cloud.

name: Midjourney
tagline: Creative platform for artistic and photorealistic image generation
description: Midjourney is a widely used AI tool that creates artistic and photorealistic images from text prompts. It is accessed through Discord and offers both free trial credits and subscription tiers.
notes: The company has not disclosed full details about its training data or bias mitigation policies.

name: DALL·E 3
tagline: Integrated text-to-image generator in ChatGPT
description: DALL·E 3, developed by OpenAI, generates high-quality visuals from text descriptions. It is integrated directly into the ChatGPT interface, allowing users to produce and edit images alongside text-based prompts.
notes: OpenAI reports that DALL·E 3 was trained on licensed and publicly available data, though detailed transparency documentation has not been released.

name: Gamma (Presentation Generator)
tagline: AI tool for automated presentation creation
description: Gamma automatically creates polished presentation decks from a short prompt or outline, allowing users to choose design themes, color palettes, and slide counts. The free version provides limited credits, with paid plans for expanded functionality.
notes: Note: Gamma's output does not easily convert to Google Slides or PowerPoint formats.

name: Canva
tagline: Integrated AI design and presentation creation suite
description: Canva integrates several AI-powered tools -- including Magic Design, Text-to-Image, and Video Assistant -- that help users create slides, social media graphics, and short videos from text prompts. Its templates and brand tools make it especially useful for students, faculty, and librarians designing instructional materials or presentations.
notes: Free for education users, though advanced AI features may require a Pro account. The company provides limited transparency about model training data.

name: LTX Studio
tagline: AI video creation platform for storyboarding and cinematic control
description: LTX Studio turns text prompts into short cinematic clips with detailed control over camera movement, lighting, and scene composition. It allows users to storyboard and edit videos directly in the platform, blending scriptwriting and visual design.
notes: Currently in early release; features may evolve as the tool develops. The company has not released full details about its training data or model transparency practices.

name: Pika Labs (Pika.art)
tagline: Browser-based text-to-video generator for creative projects
description: Pika Labs generates video clips from text or image prompts using an intuitive, browser-based interface. It supports basic video editing, style control, and motion generation, making it accessible for creative projects or instructional demonstrations.
notes: A free tier is available with limited output time, and paid plans expand rendering options. Pika has not disclosed specifics about its datasets or bias mitigation strategies.

name: Suno AI
tagline: AI music generation with customizable lyrics and style
description: Suno generates complete songs from short, descriptive prompts, allowing users to specify lyrics, tone, and musical style. The platform offers an intuitive interface and produces both instrumental and vocal tracks.
notes: Free plan with limited monthly credits, or upgrade to a paid subscription for expanded use. Suno has not disclosed details about its training data or bias mitigation practices.

name: Boomy
tagline: Quick, style-based song generation and editing tool
description: Boomy allows users to generate and edit complete songs within seconds by selecting a style, mood, or genre and providing short prompts. It's ideal for creating background music or short compositions for class projects and presentations.
notes: Free tier with limited features and clear licensing options for noncommercial use. The company has not disclosed details about its training data or bias mitigation practices.

name: Soundful
tagline: Royalty-free instrumental music creation platform
description: Soundful creates royalty-free instrumental music based on a user's chosen genre, mood, or tempo. It's particularly useful for generating background tracks for presentations, podcasts, or videos without copyright concerns.
notes: The platform provides both free and paid options, allowing downloads of short, high-quality compositions. Soundful has not published information about its model training data or transparency measures.

name: AIVA (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist)
tagline: AI composer for orchestral and cinematic music
description: AIVA composes original instrumental and orchestral music using artificial intelligence. It offers a range of styles such as cinematic, classical, and ambient. Users can customize parameters like mood, key, and tempo to create professional-sounding compositions for academic or creative projects.
notes: Includes free and paid tiers, with licensing options for educational and personal use. The company has not provided detailed documentation on its training data sources.

name: Beatoven.ai
tagline: Royalty-free soundtrack generator based on scene mood
description: Beatoven.ai generates customizable, royalty-free soundtracks by analyzing text-based mood or scene descriptions. It's designed for educators, students, and content creators who need background music for videos, podcasts, or digital storytelling.
notes: The interface allows simple adjustments to length, mood, and energy level. A free account provides limited access, and the company has not disclosed specifics about its datasets or bias mitigation policies.

name: Udio
tagline: AI-based composition and editing tool for original music
description: Udio creates original songs and instrumental tracks from descriptive text prompts. Users can refine results by genre, instrumentation, or mood, and make edits directly within the interface.
notes: The tool is currently free to use in its beta phase. Udio has not published documentation on its model training data or transparency practices.
